chapter: Friends, New York life and recording routine
title: Rent parties and chitlin' struts
summary: She went to rent parties with Fats and midnight dinners at Clarence's, and compares New York and Chicago house parties.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: Uh-huh. Well, when you were going around with Fats, did you go to rent parties then? Did they have rent parties then in New York?
You went to those with Fats?

Yeah, with Fats. (Unintelligible) with Clarence. See, Clarence was always having midnight dinners, have evening midnight dinners for us, you know, and he used to always have the whiskey by the pints, by the quarts, (unintelligible). I never did see no (unintelligible) and I wasn't much of a whiskey drinker. I'd rather drink beer, you know. I never did like whiskey much. (Unintelligible). But whiskey makes me drunk too quick. And I can't have
no fun drunk. See, beer just makes me lively , uh-huh.
Those rent parties, was there anything like that in Chicago, like those New York rent parties? Did they have anything like that in Chicago?
Yeah, Chicago with my cousin, rent party. But I never did play . I'd just go there and be a customer, you know, with my cousin. He'd buy some drinks and dance --
Well, those rent parties weren't until the '30s, were they, in the Depression? Weren't they in the '30s in the Depression?
What did they call them in Chicago when they had them in Chicago?
My cousin just told me a party. She didn't call -- she just told me we'd be going to a party. (Unintelligible) say, "Miss So-And-So got a party over there tonight," you know. (Unintelligible).
Well, it wasn't like the New York ones, to get the rent.
No. In New York, they called them chitlin' struts.
